assumptions: Analyze a valid V×V adjacency matrix with nonnegative weights, 0 meaning no edge, valid source, and O(1) primitive and heap-node comparisons. Let E be the nonzero matrix entries and n=V+E. Each settled vertex scans a full matrix row. Exclude the input matrix and returned distances array from auxiliary space. Include the O(V) output printing in runtime; it is dominated.
rationale: The exact runtime is O(V² + E log(E+1)): up to V processed vertices each scan a full matrix row, and up to E successful relaxations create heap entries with O(log(E+1)) push/pop cost. Printing adds O(V), dominated. With n=V+E the correct coarse time class is O(n²), tight for sparse connected graphs; O(n log n) would miss the V² scan cost. The returned distances array is output; processed flags use O(V) and lazy duplicate heap entries use O(E), so auxiliary space is O(V+E), coarse O(n).

The DP array initialization costs O(A); the nested amount/coin loops cost O(A·C), so time is O(A·C). The single A+1-entry array gives O(A) auxiliary space. Under n=max(A,C), the coarse classes O(n²) time and O(n) space are valid. These bounds are pseudo-polynomial in numeric amount A.

The iterative linear_search compares items until a match or the end. Its worst case examines all n elements, giving O(n) time, and it stores only the current index/item reference, giving O(1) auxiliary space. The recursive helper is outside the reviewed entrypoint.
